title: Trump's Trade Shift Sends US Stocks Soaring
text:
Following Trump’s announcement of a tariff pause, U.S. stocks experienced a dramatic surge, but is the recovery sustainable? This article delves into the market’s reaction, highlighting the key sectors that benefited from the positive news and addressing the lingering uncertainties surrounding the ongoing trade war. Discover the insights from the experts and what this means for future market behavior.
US Stocks Experience Historic Rally Following Tariff Pause Declaration Wall Street experienced a seismic shift as U.S. stocks surged following an announcement by former President Donald Trump regarding tariffs. The market, which had been teetering on edge, responded emphatically to the news of a potential shift in trade policy.
The Announcement and Immediate Market Reaction The catalyst for this dramatic upswing was Trump’s authorization of a 90-day pause on the reciprocal tariffs, with the notable exception of China. This decision, communicated via social media, ignited a buying frenzy among investors eager for clarity on the trade front.
The numbers speak volumes:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average skyrocketed by 2,963 points, a staggering 7.87%. The S&P 500 jumped by 9.52%, marking its best day since October 2008 and the third-best day since its modern inception in 1957. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite soared by an notable 12.16%, achieving its best day as January 2001 and the second-best in its history. sector-Specific Gains The positive momentum was widespread, with nearly every company in the S&P 500 experiencing gains. Several companies saw particularly significant increases:
Amazon (AMZN) Rose by 11.98%
Nike (NKE) Gained 11.36%
United Airlines (UAL) Soared 26.14%
Delta Air Lines (DAL) Surged 23.38%
American Airlines (AAL) Surged 22.6%
Apple (AAPL) Surged 15.33%
Nvidia (NVDA) Rose 18.72%
Palantir (PLTR) Gained 19%
Tesla (TSLA) surged 22.69%
Expert Analysis and Market Sentiment Market analysts suggest that the surge reflects pent-up demand for clarity amidst trade uncertainties. Chris Brigati,chief investment officer at SWBC,noted:
The market’s move upward is violent,and speaks to how badly the market was looking for clarity on this issue.
Chris Brigati, SWBC
Jamie Cox, managing partner at Harris Financial Group, highlighted the unpredictable nature of the former president’s trade policies:
Trump illustrated to everyone in the market today how incredibly tough it is to trade around his tariff regime, because he and only he knows when it ends.
Jamie Cox, Harris Financial Group
Lingering Concerns and the China Factor Despite the rally, caution remains warranted. The S&P 500, while up 12.86% from its recent low, is still down more than 3.7% from its April 2 close, preceding the initial tariff announcement.Similarly, the Nasdaq remains 2.7% below its April 2 level.
Furthermore, the trade war with China continues to escalate, with the U.S. imposing a tariff of at least 125% on Chinese goods, combining new and existing tariffs. This ongoing tension introduces a significant element of uncertainty.
Trump’s Viewpoint Former President Trump addressed the market’s reaction, both directly and indirectly. He posted on social media, urging investors to BE COOL! and declaring This is a great time to buy!!!
When questioned about whether the markets influenced his decision to pause tariffs, Trump responded:
The markets right now are extremely good.
Donald Trump
In a separate exchange, Wyoming senator John Barrasso praised Trump’s brilliance for the market’s performance. Trump responded:
Yeah, that’s up almost 7 (percentage) points, 2500 points, nobody’s ever heard of it. It’s gonna be a record.
Donald Trump
broader Economic Implications The escalating trade war has fueled fears of a potential global and U.S. economic recession.The uncertainty surrounding tariffs can lead to a slowdown in hiring and consumer spending, as businesses and consumers ultimately bear the cost of these tariffs.
Initial Market Hesitation Initially, U.S. stocks had a mixed start due to China’s retaliation and the European Union’s countermeasures against the reciprocal tariffs. However, the markets surged after the announcement that all countries, except China, would see their tariff rates revert to the worldwide 10% rate.
global Markets Rocked by Trade War Fears, Volatility Soars Key Takeaways Global markets experienced significant volatility amid concerns over trade tensions and potential recession. South Korea’s Kospi index entered bear market territory,prompting emergency support measures. Oil prices rebounded sharply after hitting multi-year lows, driven by speculation about policy responses. Investors sought refuge in conventional safe-haven assets like gold, while bond market behavior defied typical crisis patterns. The CBOE volatility index (VIX) surged to levels reminiscent of the Covid-19 pandemic and the 2008 financial crisis before retreating. Asian Markets Under Pressure Asian markets faced considerable headwinds, with South Korea’s Kospi index bearing the brunt of investor anxiety. The Kospi entered bear market territory on Wednesday, a decline of 20% from a recent peak. This prompted the South Korean government to announce $1.3 billion in emergency support measures for its auto industry, aiming to cushion the impact of potential tariffs.
Kospi Index: Closed down 1.7%, marking a 20% drop from its July 2024 peak. Taiwan Markets: Also experienced sharp declines. Shanghai Stock Market: An outlier, closing more than 1% higher amidst widespread losses in Asia. European Markets Plunge The sell-off extended into European markets, with major indices experiencing significant losses.
STOXX 600 Fell by 3.5%
France’s CAC Down 3.34%
Germany’s DAX Lower by 3%
London’s FTSE 100 Decreased by 2.92%
Oil Prices stage Dramatic Reversal Oil prices experienced a rollercoaster ride, initially plummeting to their lowest levels since 2021 before staging a significant recovery. The reversal followed speculation about potential interventions and a reassessment of the global economic outlook.
US Oil: Gained 4.65% to $62.35 a barrel after tumbling as low as $57. Brent Crude: Increased 4.23% to $65.48 a barrel, rebounding after briefly falling below $60. The initial plunge was fueled by investor fears that a potential global recession could significantly reduce demand for fuel-intensive activities like travel,transportation,and shipping.
Safe-Haven Demand Rises Amid market turmoil, investors sought refuge in traditional safe-haven assets, driving up demand and prices.
Gold: Gold spot prices rose more than 3%. Gold is frequently enough seen as a store of value during times of economic uncertainty. Bond Market Defies Expectations The bond market exhibited unusual behavior, with US Treasury yields rising even as investors typically flock to bonds during crises. This divergence suggests a complex interplay of factors influencing investor sentiment.
10-Year Treasury Yield: Rose above 4.3% after falling below 4% earlier in the week. Typically, investors pour money into longer-term bonds in times of crisis, anticipating that short-term market problems will be resolved in the long run. However, the bond market, like the stock market, has been shaken by extreme volatility in recent days, and some investors are heading for the exits.
Trump acknowledged watching the bond market’s volatility,indicating it influenced his decision to institute a 90-day pause on some tariffs. I was watching the bond market.The bond market is very tricky. I was watching it. But if you look at it now, it’s gorgeous. The bond market right now is beautiful. But yeah, I saw last night where people were getting a little queasy, he said.
Deutsche Bank analysts suggested that the mass exodus from Treasury bonds might signal weakening demand for US-backed assets, which are traditionally viewed as the gold standard for safety due to the backing of the US government.
In a trade war, investors may fear that america could lose its special standing in the world. JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon echoed this sentiment in his shareholder letter earlier this week. Foreign governments negotiating with Trump on trade may threaten to sell off their massive Treasury hoards, hurting America’s ability to borrow money to pay for its significant budget deficit.
Dollar Weakness Signals concerns The US dollar index, which measures the dollar’s strength against six foreign currencies, pared its losses after initially sliding on Wednesday. The dollar has broadly weakened this year — a potential warning sign about waning investor confidence in the United States.
Volatility Index Calms After Surge The CBOE volatility index, also known as the “VIX” and Wall Street’s “fear gauge,” sank 35.75% after Trump’s announcement of a pause on most reciprocal tariffs, reflecting easing jitters among traders.
VIX Peak: Briefly surpassed 50 points Wednesday morning, a level associated with extreme volatility. Historical Context: The index had closed above 50 on Tuesday, a level reached only twice before this week: during the early stages of the Covid pandemic in March and April 2020 and the 2008-2009 financial crisis. The VIX measures expected price fluctuations or volatility in the S&P 500 Index options over the next 30 days. The VIX often surges on days when the broader market sinks — and rallies when stocks rise. But over time, the VIX tends to be lower in bull markets and higher when the bears are in control.
Volatility works in both directions, and this week is a good example. The market bounced and tanked and surged as news — and even some fake news Monday — about Trump’s potential plans for tariffs made its way through Wall Street.
Trade War Uncertainty Persists Despite Tariff Pause Market Overview: A Skittish Landscape Investors are experiencing heightened anxiety amid ongoing trade tensions between the U.S. and China.
President Trump’s recent announcement to pause most reciprocal tariffs initially sparked optimism. However, underlying concerns about a protracted trade war continue to fuel market volatility. Expert Analysis: A Trade War Standoff Susannah Streeter, head of money and markets at Hargreaves Lansdown, offers insights into the current situation:
The US and China are now locked into a trade war without either likely to back down at the moment.
Susannah Streeter, Hargreaves Lansdown
Ms. Streeter further elaborates on investor behavior:
What you’re seeing in investors being extremely skittish which is why (there are) big fluctuations.
Susannah Streeter, Hargreaves Lansdown
economic Implications: Lingering Concerns The potential for a prolonged trade war raises several economic concerns:
Disruptions to global supply chains. Increased costs for businesses and consumers. Reduced economic growth in both the U.S.and China. Looking Ahead: Navigating Uncertainty Investors should remain vigilant and prepared for continued market fluctuations as the U.S.-China trade situation evolves.
Diversification and a long-term investment strategy are crucial for weathering potential storms.
